title: On Marching past the old hall at noon
subtitle: 战争和平 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）
meta: 主题语境：战争和平（历史社会与文化·战争与和平）　|　核心词汇：march　|　正文 353 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 march 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1993 the planner ① marched past the old hall at noon at once, and every citizen in the district said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three years on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the planner ② marches past the old hall at noon in the rain without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ march past the old hall at noon at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ marched past the old hall at noon before — a line in the report for March 1987 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Marching past the old hall at noon at once, the planner said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the plan at the far square, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ march the prisoners to the gate in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ March the prisoners to the gate at once and never mention it again.

By 2000 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the report, and a new citizen from the next district ⑧ marches the prisoners to the gate at once every year without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the square, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ marched past the old hall at noon again when nobody else would.

⑩ To march past the old hall at noon, my mother said in 2005, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the district remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the district forgets, somebody marches past the old hall at noon in the rain again and somebody must march past the old hall at noon at once all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 行进（一般过去式 marched past the old hall at noon：1993 年规划员头一回这样做，二话不说地）
B. v. 行进（一般现在 marches past the old hall at noon：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 行进（不定式 to march past the old hall at noon：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 行进（过去完成时 had marched past the old hall at noon：1987 年三月的规划报告上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 行进（动名词 marching past the old hall at noon 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 迫使…走（march the prisoners to the gate：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去迫使…走把俘虏押到门口）
G. v. 迫使…走（march the prisoners to the gate：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 行进（后段两处：新来的市民照例 marches the prisoners to the gate，而母亲又一次 marched past the old hall at noon）

answers.why: march 意为“行进”，1993 年规划员二话不说地行进正午从老厅前列队走过，那是街区里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 marched。
march 意为“行进”，自那以后规划员淋着雨把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 marches。
march 意为“行进”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯行进正午从老厅前列队走过”，此处为不定式 to march past the old hall at noon。
march 意为“行进”，规划报告里 三月 那行字说明早在 2000 年之前就有人行进过，故用过去完成时 had marched。
march 意为“行进”，规划员说“行进正午从老厅前列队走过这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 marching past the old hall at noon 作主语。
march 意为“迫使…走”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去迫使…走把俘虏押到门口”，should ever 之后用原形 march the prisoners to the gate。
march 意为“迫使…走”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻迫使…走把俘虏押到门口（march the prisoners to the gate at once），以后再也不要提起。
march 意为“行进”，新来的市民每个年份都照例迫使…走把俘虏押到门口，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 marches。
march 意为“行进”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次二话不说地行进正午从老厅前列队走过，用一般过去式 marched 叙述。
march 意为“行进”，结尾那句是母亲 2005 年的话：要行进正午从老厅前列队走过，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和街区记住的那一件。

Three years on, the planner still marches past the old hall at noon in the rain without being asked.
My mother said later that to march past the old hall at noon at all was the part nobody had expected.
Somebody had marched past the old hall at noon long before 2000, and the line in the report for March proves it.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 march 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1993 the planner marched past the old hall at noon at once, and nobody in the district forgot it.
Even now the planner marches past the old hall at noon in the rain whenever the district asks.
Marching past the old hall at noon at once, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever march the prisoners to the gate in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new citizen from the next district marches the prisoners to the gate at once every year, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother marched past the old hall at noon again, and the district remembered that half.
